# AOSP PinyinIME decoder provenance

Upstream: Android Open Source Project, `platform/packages/inputmethods/PinyinIME`.

- Official repository: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/inputmethods/PinyinIME/
- Mirror used for retrieval: https://github.com/oxangen/PinyinIME
- Pinned mirror revision: `05cc8f8f2465553bc6d19b2ede24073d079eeed7`
- Mirror identifies itself as a copy of the official AOSP project. Its final commit only adds its README. Source copyright headers identify the Android Open Source Project.
- Retrieved on 2026-10-04. Official Gitiles was used to verify project/API/license; direct official-host cloning and archive downloads timed out in the current network. GitHub CLI also failed with a TLS handshake timeout. GitHub codeload succeeded.
- Imported components: `jni/include/*.h`, `jni/share/*.cpp`, `res/raw/dict_pinyin.dat`, and project `NOTICE`.
- License: Apache License 2.0, retained in [NOTICE](NOTICE) and upstream file headers. The official project includes `MODULE_LICENSE_APACHE2`.
- Original dictionary (v0.4 baseline): `res/raw/dict_pinyin.dat`, 1,068,442 bytes, SHA-256 `6bf0bbde4e3134cce38d08524a9f4dc1af40435243c8e36b38eb68d1e14462b2`. v0.5 replaces this system model as described below.
- Original downloaded master ZIP SHA-256: `ffa3289caf1559ed831a5a7a087ea17c5a317142134d6fdc9c46eae1413820b2`.
- Verified pinned-revision ZIP SHA-256: `6cfb6b3cf7add8a35a30baab18010b1c2ebe801186150d7a72e6c6f6c6f401e1`. Every imported header/source matched the pinned revision before the documented patches.

Qingyu modifications to imported sources:

1. `dictlist.h` / `dictlist.cpp`: dictionary count and serialized sizes explicitly use 32-bit fields, including the previously 64-bit-dependent save path.
2. `matrixsearch.h` / `matrixsearch.cpp`: learning-enabled flag prevents new user lemmas and frequency updates while disabled. Skipping a lifecycle flush alone would not suffice because upstream can flush automatically while learning.
3. `pinyinime.h` / `pinyinime.cpp`: public native setter for that flag.
4. `compat/cutils/log.h` is a separate compatibility shim using the public NDK log API. The original Android system-private JNI service and libcutils are not linked.
5. `matrixsearch.cpp::get_lpis`: shared candidate/deduplication scratch space is bounded using actual struct sizes on each ABI. Dense abbreviated input previously triggered a debug assertion or discarded candidates in release mode; the adapter now keeps the best-scored candidates that fit.
6. `dictbuilder.cpp` (offline compiler only): remove the historical four-character and frequency-60 admission filters. The native format already supports eight-character words. Allocate enough deep trie nodes for eight-character input and reject more than 65,535 character/reading index items rather than silently overflowing the serialized 16-bit index.
7. `dicttrie.cpp` / `matrixsearch.cpp`: retain the original 100 milestone / 600 parsing-mark capacities and safely stop new paths when full. Count only marks actually allocated when publishing an extension handle; the upstream second/deeper-level loops counted unallocated marks and could publish an out-of-bounds handle. Exhaustion is an ordinary bounded-search condition, including root paths, rather than an assertion that aborts the IME. Original letters and existing paths remain available.

The native workspace retains the original 40-step bound. JNI supplies at most 39 pinyin characters and nine syllables per native search, using AOSP's own spelling parser before lattice expansion, while the Java adapter preserves up to 64 requested characters and continues remaining segments. Expanding the workspace alone was rejected after a pathological repeated-vowel boundary test reached native pool limits. Pre-parsing the syllable bound avoids filling those pools before the engine's normal post-search truncation runs.

## v0.5 system model and indexed companion

The native decoder, incremental lattice, prefix selection, abbreviated input, prediction and user-dictionary implementation remain AOSP. The system model is rebuilt with a modern lexicon; the platform-neutral adapter also merges exact readings and bounded complete sentence paths from a local indexed companion. Glosses are independent from Chinese ranking and can fail without delaying or disabling Chinese input.

- Modern source: [Rime Ice](https://github.com/iDvel/rime-ice), pinned revision `da1fbe602e38f26db846fa10120ee64c2b0324c0`, `cn_dicts/base.dict.yaml` and `cn_dicts/ext.dict.yaml`. The upstream project declares GPL-3.0-only. Source URLs, SHA-256 hashes and retained source headers are in [model-v2-manifest.json](model-v2-manifest.json), [RIME-ICE-SOURCE-HEADER.txt](RIME-ICE-SOURCE-HEADER.txt) and [RIME-ICE-EXT-SOURCE-HEADER.txt](RIME-ICE-EXT-SOURCE-HEADER.txt). The complete [Rime-ice-LICENSE](Rime-ice-LICENSE) is also included in the APK licenses assets. No separate Tencent dictionary is imported.
- Retained source: AOSP's 65,105 raw word readings at the same decoder revision, SHA-256 `408700f28a56091fa07f3b849a0f134fbfc71e6b2ae9b3f52973a5b076f599ff`.
- Companion fallback: the project's pinned CC-CEDICT snapshot, retaining its CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution and [manifest](../cedict/manifest.json). It supplies only missing readings with a low source prior; it is not a neural context model.
- Rebuilt model: `app/src/main/assets/pinyin/dict_pinyin.dat`, 4,539,440 bytes, SHA-256 `ae80997b6e2b2de23bc11276767a15cd00b1e8e6308823a2761769d811a3513a`. The prepared raw input contains 235,000 readings and 233,642 unique words. The compiler admits 234,996 readings after excluding four legacy syllabic-interjection rows it cannot serialize. This is below the 240,000 lemma allocation and the system/user lemma-ID boundary.
- Indexed companion: `app/src/main/assets/pinyin/lexicon-v2.db`, 599,320 readings, 67,260,416 uncompressed bytes, SHA-256 `ef4c9c9f22deea61e02a0cdf71ad6be2e906af3088f0d3abd2657385034ad4ff`. SQLite indexes on normalized full pinyin, initials and word text avoid a full-dictionary scan on each key. APK compression and first-run installation are separate from the uncompressed file size.

The reproducible transformation is in `tools/build_pinyin_dictionary.py` and `tools/build-pinyin-model.ps1`: preserve old legal readings and spelling alphabet; globally select modern readings by upstream frequency with a threefold admission priority for two-character words; share the maximum source weight among a word's readings; map `lve/nve` to AOSP's `lue/nue`; reject invalid spellings, mismatched character/syllable counts, non-BMP/non-Chinese text and words longer than eight characters. No test-specific word patches or weights are used. Native legacy-only counts receive a uniform 0.15 fallback prior; complete native single-syllable characters retain the first position ahead of alternate multi-syllable lexical splits in the adapter.

All 413 serialized full-spelling IDs retain their original ordering. Model v2's character/reading index has 17,102 compiled items; its largest deep-node sibling count is 142 and its largest multi-syllable homophone count is 31, within the serialized 16/8-bit bounds. The existing 39-character, nine-syllable native search guard remains; up to 64 original letters are preserved by the Java adapter. A sentence path uses at most 160 indexed word-graph edges, three paths per boundary and 24 Chinese characters. A code containing `lve/nve` can additionally query the legacy `lue/nue` equivalent; canonical syllables are checked before removing separators, and the original code path is retained, so `nv'er/nver` is not rewritten. Known exact words skip that path search, and unfinished single-letter input remains native-only. A failed local provider always falls back to native candidates.

The service installs the new system model under a new `pinyin-v2.dat` filename and retains `user-pinyin.dat`. System lemma IDs may change with the model; AOSP user lemmas use their own ID range, stored text and spelling IDs, so system lemma IDs are not transplanted into the user file. `tools/test-chinese-upgrade.ps1` creates an actual custom phrase with the original model, flushes and reopens it with both models, and verifies spelling, complete commit and byte-preserving disabled learning. Local full/initials/context learning is separate, bounded and follows the user's privacy setting. Finishing a previously selected prefix also learns the complete selected phrase once under its original full code; canonical readings come from indexed selected words and native syllable boundaries. Segmented native prefixes retain those readings. Selecting one whole word remains a single learning event; preview and disabled learning never increment counts.

`tools/test-chinese-quality.ps1` exercises actual Java/JNI and Android SQLite: incremental typing, candidate rank, complete preview, unchanged snapshot, commit and continuous deletion. `-Baseline -Dictionary .tools/pinyin-model/dict-v0.4.dat` explicitly uses the original binary. The raw per-case reports retain failures: frequency-only sentence composition can still choose semantically wrong homophones or boundaries for unseen phrases, which requires corpus-backed context scoring rather than manual test-word boosts.
